frontier.note: FRONTIER WITHDRAWN — ERCOT reverts to NOT-YET (owner directive 2026-07-17, the ERCOT-79 availability-envelope audit: 'we can't have a keeper on inaccurate data'). The 2026-07-17 frontier declaration rested on a keeper (ercot76) whose scarcity tail was formed on a PHANTOM CAMPD facility-outage bug: the run-based detector hard-zeroed ~1.9-5.7 GW of daily-cycling combined-cycle capability its own CEMS shows generating (T H Wharton et al.), artificially exhausting the event-time fleet so the co-opt priced into its ORDC steps. ERCOT-79 found and fixed the detector (event-based detection for cycling classes; source-faithful, measured CEMS + EIA-930, validated 58h false-outage 1,904->0 MW/h, 0% genuine-outage over-correction) and the fix was ADOPTED (corrected campd-outages.csv installed). On the corrected fleet the keeper recipe (re-solved as keeper 2026-07-17-ercot79-corrected-outages) resolves the 2023 summer over-shoot ($1,068->$242, confirming ERCOT-78) but UN-CATCHES the real scarcity tail (2023 C3c 179->53 vs RT 181, Aug caught 71->25, 2025 tail 19->0) — the offer/scarcity calibration was tuned against the phantom-tightened fleet. DETERMINATION: NOT-YET (C3a/C3b/C3c fail on accurate data). OPEN LANE (successor): a full ERCOT offer-curve + ORDC/co-opt re-calibration against the corrected availability envelope, so the real scarcity re-forms on real fleet tightness. CROSS-ISO: the detector is shared — PJM's committed facility csv shows a stronger phantom signature and all six ISOs' unit-level extracts use it; each ISO is its own regenerate-and-re-audit lane. See results/calibration/FINDING-ercot79-phantom-outage-2026-07.md.
